authority.non_authority_statement: This active inventory grants no accepted-decision, implementation, or activation authority.

lifecycle.terminal_handling: Remove resolved, rejected, or superseded records in the same bounded package that records their accepted ADR, canonical rationale, or explicit rejection; preserve history in Git and linked Issues rather than in a second permanent archive.

records.blocking_owner_question: Select ADR 0036 Option A (recommended explicit deferral until a named consumer exists), Option B (public read-only v1 first), or Option C (authenticated first-party account/client v1 first).
records.decision_question: Should Oteryn activate a general Platform API now, and if so which consumer class should establish the first stable surface?

DERIVED: A speculative broad API would create security and compatibility commitments before a named consumer exists, contrary to the current concrete-consumer-first module boundary.

Existing Passport-backed API authentication is reusable implementation capability for specialized game-auth, but it is not evidence that a general authenticated API product, scopes model or token lifecycle has been accepted.
PROVEN: PlatformAPI is PLANNED and canonical module architecture says to expose endpoints only for a concrete client/use case while reusing module application services and policies.

Current routes/api.php exposes only POST /v1/game-auth/tickets and current routes/internal.php exposes only private Gateway game-auth contracts; canonical architecture explicitly excludes them from general PlatformAPI classification.
Portal work allocation marks Platform API ARCHITECTURE_READY / DECISION_REQUIRED for the first public surface, and Issue 490 retains PlatformAPI as a residual open finding.
UNKNOWN: Whether the repository owner wants explicit deferral, a public read-only v1 first surface, or an authenticated first-party account/client v1 first surface.
Exact future resource inventory, authentication/scopes, rate budgets and compatibility/deprecation windows depend on the selected consumer posture and implementation design.

options.description: Keep the general Platform API explicitly deferred until an approved named consumer/use case exists, while preserving specialized game-auth/internal contracts outside PlatformAPI classification and enforcing a fail-closed activation checklist before the first stable endpoint.
options.title: Defer general Platform API until a named consumer exists
trade_offs: Lowest security and compatibility surface and best match for the current concrete-consumer-first architecture.
No general public/first-party API is available immediately; a future consumer requires a separate activation package.

options.description: Activate a stable anonymous/read-only v1 over explicitly approved already-public application queries/read models with public enumeration/privacy, freshness, cache, pagination, abuse/rate-limit and compatibility policy.
options.title: Public read-only v1 first
trade_offs: Lower authorization complexity than a private API and useful for machine-readable public capabilities.
Creates public scraping/enumeration, availability and compatibility commitments before a named consumer has demonstrated need.

options.description: Activate a stable authenticated API for an identified first-party Oteryn client using source-module application services and a purpose-designed client/scopes/token lifecycle rather than inheriting game-auth ticket semantics.
options.title: Authenticated first-party account/client v1 first
trade_offs: Directly supports future native/desktop/mobile owner-private workflows.
Largest accepted-option security/privacy burden, including token theft/revocation, client trust, scopes, device/session and compatibility decisions.

options.description: Expose a broad mixed public and authenticated v1 spanning many modules before a concrete consumer boundary is selected.
options.title: Broad mixed API now
trade_offs: Rejected baseline because it maximizes attack surface, duplicated orchestration risk and long-lived compatibility commitments.

records.problem_statement: The repository has specialized API-shaped game-auth/internal transports but no accepted general Platform API product surface. Issue 490 requires an explicit disposition, while current architecture forbids treating specialized routes or speculative endpoints as general API completeness.
records.recommendation: Adopt Option A. Explicitly defer the general Platform API until a named consumer exists, retain specialized game-auth/internal contracts outside PlatformAPI classification, and require the ADR 0036 activation checklist before the first stable endpoint.
records.title: Platform API activation and first-surface policy
